doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Joe Henderson and why it is never the instrument's fault
summary: Cracked notes are just sounds; Harris recalls Joe Henderson sounding magic with any drummer and lifting everyone.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I have the improviser’s mindset so that I’ve shown up and there were cracked notes, but in the concert I’ll use those notes. A note is just another sound that I can use in the process of improvisation. So — I remember playing with Joe Henderson and a couple of us in the band, Joe was going through a period where he was trying out a bunch of drummers. And on occasion he’d try someone who really didn’t work out. So some of us were young, we were in the back and we were talking like, “Oh man, this guy messed up my solo, and I was trying to do this” and such and such. But Joe Henderson, night after night, it didn’t matter who was on the stage, he was able to be magic, with unbelievable clarity regardless of the level of the other musicians around him. And in fact he elevated everyone else because when he started playing everybody else sounded better. So that’s a great lesson I think I learned over the years from playing with Joe Henderson that it’s never the instrument’s fault.
You can take that instrument in your right hand, they’ll make magic with it.
